encounters.cc: Severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain for 8 hours

lines: Severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain for 8 hours
She presents to the emergency department with severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain that started 8 hours ago.
The pain is sharp, constant, and worsens with movement.
She denies any nausea, vomiting, or changes in bowel habits.
Her last menstrual period was 3 weeks ago and was normal.
- Opioid use disorder, sustained remission on medication-assisted therapy
- Laparoscopic appendectomy with abscess drainage (age 33, postpartum)
- Left salpingectomy for ruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy
- Sumatriptan 50 mg oral PRN migraine headache (max 200 mg/day)
- Prenatal vitamin with folate 1 tablet daily
She has no known drug allergies.
With a history of intravenous heroin use, currently in a methadone maintenance program,
On examination, her temperature is 38.2°C (100.8°F), blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, pulse is 95/min, and respiratory rate is 18/min.
Abdominal examination reveals tenderness and rebound tenderness in the right lower quadrant.
There is no guarding or rigidity.
White blood cell count is 12,000/µL with 80% neutrophils.
Abdominal ultrasound shows a normal gallbladder, liver, and kidneys, but there is a 3 cm fluid-filled structure in the right adnexa with surrounding free fluid.

encounters.cc: Acting increasingly strange and confused 10 days after delivering first child

lines: Acting increasingly strange and confused 10 days after delivering first child

This 32-year-old female with a history of opioid use disorder in sustained remission on methadone maintenance, treated previously in this emergency department for acute appendicitis, presents 10 days following the delivery of her first child.
Her husband reports that she has not been sleeping and has been acting increasingly strange since the delivery.
She has been heard talking to herself and seems to be responding to voices that no one else can hear.
She has expressed beliefs that the baby is possessed and needs to be protected from evil spirits.
- Opioid use disorder, sustained remission on medication-assisted therapy
She had an uncomplicated pregnancy and vaginal delivery.
- Laparoscopic appendectomy with abscess drainage (age 33, postpartum)
- Left salpingectomy for ruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy
- Sumatriptan 50 mg oral PRN migraine headache (max 200 mg/day)
- Prenatal vitamin with folate 1 tablet daily
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 4 years ago prior to conception of first child.
Alcohol: None; sober from alcohol since initiating substance use treatment.
Occupation: Administrative assistant at a local community college.
Her vital signs are within normal limits.
On examination, she is agitated, appears to be preoccupied with internal stimuli, and is not oriented to time or place.

encounters.cc: Difficulty sleeping, shakiness, and increased anxiety 6 weeks postpartum

lines: Difficulty sleeping, shakiness, and increased anxiety 6 weeks postpartum
The patient presents to the Endocrinology clinic for evaluation six weeks postpartum.

She has a known history of postpartum thyroiditis and prior postpartum psychosis following her first delivery, and she was seen earlier today in Obstetrics & Gynecology for her routine postpartum examination.
She delivered a full-term healthy infant 6 weeks ago and has been breastfeeding without complications.
Over the last two weeks, she has noticed feeling unusually restless, with frequent palpitations and difficulty concentrating.
She denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or recent illness.
Her appetite is normal, but she has noticed her clothes fitting more loosely despite no efforts to lose weight.
She has no neck pain or tenderness, and no visual complaints.
- Opioid use disorder, sustained remission on medication-assisted therapy
- Laparoscopic appendectomy with abscess drainage (age 33, postpartum)
- Left salpingectomy for ruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy
- Sumatriptan 50 mg oral PRN migraine headache (max 200 mg/day)
- Prenatal vitamin with folate 1 tablet daily
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 4 years ago prior to conception of first child.
Alcohol: None; sober from alcohol since initiating substance use treatment.
Occupation: Administrative assistant at a local community college.
On physical exam, she has a fine tremor in both hands and a heart rate of 102/min.
The thyroid gland is slightly enlarged and firm but non-tender.
There is no evidence of lid lag or exophthalmos.
Thyroid function testing shows elevated free T4 and suppressed TSH
A radioactive iodine uptake scan reveals low uptake.

encounters.cc: Gradually enlarging lump in right breast while breastfeeding

lines: Gradually enlarging lump in right breast while breastfeeding
This 33-year-old with opioid use disorder in remission on methadone, history of postpartum psychosis and thyroiditis, presents six months postpartum.
She delivered vaginally without complications and has been exclusively breastfeeding.
She reports a gradually enlarging, mildly uncomfortable swelling in the outer quadrant of her right breast that does not fluctuate in size with feeding.
She denies fever, chills, or nipple discharge.
- Opioid use disorder, sustained remission on medication-assisted therapy
- Laparoscopic appendectomy with abscess drainage (age 33, postpartum)
- Left salpingectomy for ruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy

- Prenatal vitamin with folate 1 tablet daily

encounters.cc: Acute onset of left lower abdominal pain with vaginal spotting

lines: Acute onset of left lower abdominal pain with vaginal spotting
This 33-year-old female with history of migraine, postpartum psychosis, thyroiditis, and opioid use disorder in remission on methadone presents with acute abdominal pain.
Nine months postpartum following contraceptive counseling, she reports that the pain is sharp, located on the left side, and began suddenly 4 hours ago.
She also mentions that she has had light vaginal spotting for the past two days.
Her last menstrual period was 6 weeks ago, and she has a regular 28-day cycle.
She has been breastfeeding her 9-month-old child and has not yet resumed contraception.
- Opioid use disorder, sustained remission on medication-assisted therapy
- Laparoscopic appendectomy with abscess drainage (age 33, postpartum)
- Left salpingectomy for ruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy
- Sumatriptan 50 mg oral PRN migraine headache (max 200 mg/day)
- Prenatal vitamin with folate 1 tablet daily
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 4 years ago prior to conception of first child.
Alcohol: None; sober from alcohol since initiating substance use treatment.
Occupation: Administrative assistant at a local community college.
Her vital signs are as follows: blood pressure 90/60 mmHg, heart rate 120 beats per minute, respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute, and temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F).
On examination, she appears anxious and is in distress.
Abdominal examination reveals left lower quadrant tenderness with rebound tenderness.
A pelvic examination shows a closed cervical os with no active bleeding, but there is tenderness during movement of the cervix.
A bedside ultrasound reveals an empty uterus and a complex adnexal mass on the left side with moderate free fluid in the pelvis.

encounters.cc: Abdominal pain localized to right lower quadrant 3 weeks after second delivery

lines: Abdominal pain localized to right lower quadrant 3 weeks after second delivery
The patient is a 39-year-old female, now 3 weeks postpartum after her second vaginal delivery, with a history of acute appendicitis in 2020, postpartum psychosis, and ruptured ectopic pregnancy.
She gave birth to her second child 3 weeks ago via normal vaginal delivery.
The pain initially started around her umbilicus but has now localized to the right lower quadrant.
She also reports a low-grade fever, nausea, and a single episode of vomiting.
Her appetite has decreased since the onset of pain.
She denies any urinary symptoms, vaginal discharge, or bleeding.
